title: Skiing by train from London: which resorts you can reach in a day
author: Brogan
cover_image_alt: A small blue and white train on a snowy track between snow-laden trees, with white mountains behind
intro: The easiest ski resorts to reach by train from London are in the French Alps around Bourg-Saint-Maurice and Moûtiers, served by Eurostar's Saturday snow train in about eight hours. Chamonix, Zermatt, Verbier and St Anton take longer, with a change or two. Here's how each works.
seo_title: Ski by train from London: 8 hrs to the Alps (2026/27)
seo_description: Eurostar's Saturday snow train reaches Moûtiers and Bourg-Saint-Maurice in about 8 hours, 19 Dec 2026 to 20 Feb 2027. Plus sleepers and Swiss options.

sections.heading: The short answer
sections.text:
- **Fastest:** Eurostar Snow, about 8 hrs
- **Season:** 19 Dec 2026 to 20 Feb 2027
- **Overnight:** Travelski Night Express
- **Best resorts by train:** Les Arcs, Val Thorens

We checked the 2026/27 timetables in November 2026. Dates, stops and prices change each season, so book through Eurostar or a rail booking site and check the details before you plan your week.

sections.heading: Why go by train
sections.text:
A ski week by train starts in central London rather than at an airport at dawn. There's no transfer coach queue at Geneva or Chambéry, no worrying about the weight of your ski bag, and you watch the Alps arrive from your seat.

It can also be quicker door to door than it looks. A morning flight to Geneva still needs a journey to the airport, two hours there beforehand and a transfer of two to three hours on a busy Saturday. The snow train drops you in the valley, and some resorts are a short bus or funicular ride from the station.

Tip: on Eurostar, skis and snowboards can go as part of your normal luggage allowance, rather than as a paid extra as on most flights. Check the size and weight rules before you go.

sections.heading: Eurostar Snow: the Saturday ski train
sections.text:
Eurostar's ski service runs on **Saturdays from 19 December 2026 to 20 February 2027**, from London St Pancras to the Tarentaise valley, with a change of train at Lille. Return trains run on Sundays and some Saturdays until 28 February. The journey takes just under eight hours.

It stops at **Chambéry**, **Albertville**, **Moûtiers**, **Aime-la-Plagne**, **Landry** and **Bourg-Saint-Maurice**, which between them serve some of the biggest ski areas in the world.

Watch out: the season is short, and it doesn't cover the February half term for every school, or Easter. Book early, as the trains sell out for the busiest weeks.

sections.heading: Which resort from which station
sections.image_alt: A railway line through deep snow above Zermatt, with jagged white peaks under a blue sky
sections.image_caption: In Switzerland, trains run right into resorts like Zermatt, which is car-free.
sections.text:
| Station | Resorts | Last leg |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bourg-Saint-Maurice | Les Arcs | Funicular, about 7 minutes |
| Bourg-Saint-Maurice | Tignes, Val d'Isère | Bus |
| Moûtiers | [Val Thorens](/destinations/val-thorens), Méribel, Courchevel | Bus |
| Aime-la-Plagne | La Plagne | Bus |
| Landry | Peisey-Vallandry | Bus |

Les Arcs is the easiest of all: the funicular from Bourg-Saint-Maurice takes you up to Arc 1600, and you can be on the slopes the afternoon you arrive. [Val Thorens](/destinations/val-thorens), the highest resort in the Three Valleys, is about an hour's bus ride from Moûtiers.

sections.heading: Overnight: the Travelski Night Express
sections.text: The **Travelski Night Express** is a sleeper train to the same valley. It started from Paris in the 2025/26 season, and a second route from Amsterdam and Brussels is planned for 2026/27, on Friday nights from mid-December to late March. From London, you take an afternoon Eurostar to Paris or Brussels and board the sleeper that evening, then wake up near the resorts on Saturday morning. Travelski sells it mainly as part of a package with accommodation and lift passes, so it suits people booking a whole ski week in one go.

sections.heading: Switzerland and Austria
sections.text:
The Swiss and Austrian resorts take longer, but the trains go right to the door:

- **[Zermatt](/destinations/zermatt):** Eurostar to Paris, a TGV Lyria to Lausanne or Geneva, then Swiss trains via Visp. Zermatt is car-free, so the train is the natural way in.
- **[Verbier](/destinations/verbier):** the same way to Martigny, then a train to Le Châble and the gondola up.
- **[St Anton](/destinations/st-anton):** Eurostar to Paris, a TGV to Zurich, then an Austrian train to St Anton station, in the village.

These journeys usually take 11 to 13 hours with two or three changes, so many people stop overnight in Paris or Zurich on the way.

sections.heading: Chamonix by train
sections.text:
[Chamonix](/destinations/chamonix) is reached via Paris, with a TGV to Saint-Gervais and the little Mont-Blanc Express train up the valley, or via Geneva. Expect around 10 to 12 hours from London with good connections.

It's a good choice for a mixed group, since Chamonix is a real town with plenty to do off the slopes, and the train runs along the valley between the ski areas.

sections.heading: How to choose
sections.text:
- **For the easiest trip:** Les Arcs on the Saturday Eurostar.
- **For the biggest ski area:** Val Thorens or Méribel, via Moûtiers.
- **For the snowiest late season:** Val Thorens or Tignes, which are high enough for March and April.
- **For a car-free village:** Zermatt.
- **For a night on the train:** the Travelski Night Express.

Our post on the [best ski resorts for a weekend from the UK](/blog/best-ski-resorts-for-a-weekend-from-the-uk) covers short trips, and the [ski holidays](/destinations/ski-holidays) and [train holidays](/destinations/train-holidays) pages have more ideas. Can't agree on a resort? Read our guide to [deciding where to go on holiday](/how-to-decide-where-to-go-on-holiday), or add your shortlist to somewhere.party and let the draw decide.

faqs.question: Is there a direct ski train from London?
faqs.answer: Eurostar's Saturday ski service runs from London St Pancras to the French Alps in about eight hours, with a change of train at Lille. In 2026/27 it runs from 19 December to 20 February.

faqs.question: Which ski resorts can you reach by train from London?
faqs.answer: The easiest are in the Tarentaise valley: Les Arcs, La Plagne, Tignes, Val d'Isère, Val Thorens, Méribel and Courchevel. Zermatt, Verbier, St Anton and Chamonix take longer, with changes.

faqs.question: Can you take skis on Eurostar?
faqs.answer: Yes. Skis and snowboards can travel as part of your luggage allowance. Check Eurostar's current size and weight rules before you go.

faqs.question: Is there a sleeper train to the Alps from the UK?
faqs.answer: Not directly. The Travelski Night Express runs from Paris, with a route from Brussels and Amsterdam planned for 2026/27, so you take Eurostar to join it.
